_about.what: The numbers of a fleet action fought out on the field (src/battle/sea). Every ship's weight, toughness and nation's quality come from data/campaign/navy.json, as the rules count them: this file only says how the field plays them out. Abstract by design (project memory air-battle-paused, ruling 217): pieces wear each other down by range and angle; nothing is aimed and nothing flies.
_about.field: The sea is a square of 'size' metres. The attacker's fleets come on from the south edge, 'edge' metres in, the defender's from the north. 'limit' is the battle time in seconds before it is called on the exchange so far.
_about.classes: speed in metres a second at cruising speed; turn in radians a second at full way (a ship turns slower when slow, and barely at all when stopped); best is the range at which a class hits hardest and reach the furthest it hits at all; per is how many ships of the class sail as one piece (destroyers in fours); crew is a ship's company, for the after-action card only; len and beam are a ship's length and breadth in metres, for the screens and the 3D models; a piece's ships sail in line ahead, three lengths apart. A carrier fights by its strike, not its guns: standoff is how far it keeps from the nearest enemy, behind its own screen, so that the heavy guns can still reach it and it pays for its place in the line as the rules count it. punch evens out what the reach of a class costs it: destroyers have to close before they can fire at all, so on the field each destroyer's weight hits harder, and a fleet strong in destroyers is worth what the rules say it is.
_about.speeds: Shares of a class's cruising speed for the speed order, and accel, how fast way is gained or lost (metres a second, each second).
_about.fire: rate turns weight into wear on a hull each second. hull: a side's hulls together come to this many times its weight, shared over its ships by the rules' toughness (a battleship takes about twice the wear of its weight that a destroyer does), so that toughness decides which ships go down and not who wins. far is what a piece does at the edge of its reach, against 1 at its best range or closer. endOn is what its guns do when the target is dead ahead or astern, against 1 on the beam: crossing the T. damaged: a crippled ship still fights at this share. retarget: seconds between a piece looking for a new target.
_about.nerve: A piece's nerve falls by 'hit' for each whole hull it takes in wear, and by 'near' when a ship of its own side goes down within 'nearR' metres; out of the fight for 'quiet' seconds it mends at 'mend' a second. Below 'waver' it wavers and fights at 'wavering'; below 'break' it breaks off for its own edge.
_about.side: A side breaks off when it has lost 'breakAt' of its ships' weight (a share of 'spread' either way, more with a good admiral: 'admiral' a level). After a side breaks, its enemy has 'pursuit' seconds to make it pay before the battle ends. The luck of the day is the rules' own: one roll of the dice's run (0.8 to 1.2, navy.ts seaBattles) for the battle, the attacker's ships fighting that much better and the defender's that much worse, so that with nobody playing the field gives what the dice give.
_about.strike: A carrier's strike: ordered, it lands 'windup' seconds later on the target and the ships near it within 'radius', and the carrier can strike again 'every' seconds after that. A strike carries the weight of 'every' seconds of the carrier's own weight at 'share': a gun ship, out of reach some of the time and at long range or end-on much of the rest, deals about a third of its full rate over an action, so a carrier that strikes whenever it can pulls its weight as the rules count it, no more. It takes the same weight out of the fight whatever ship it falls on (wear in proportion to the ship's hull), so the screen is no cheaper a target than the battleship; share 0.255 keeps carriers within the dice with that (ruling 226, 4). It is counted, not flown: no aircraft are on the field.
_about.air: Aircraft from the coasts (the rules' airOver, times navy.json air.weight) raid every 'every' seconds, the first within the first raid's span; each raid's weight is 'share' of what that much weight of guns would deal in the time, as a strike's is.
_about.pieces: No more than 'most' pieces a side: past that, cruisers sail in twos, then destroyers in more than fours.
_about.ai: The computer's captains (and the player's, where he has given no order): a ship further than 'keep' metres from the middle of its own fleet works back toward it as it fights. A ship ordered to attack fires on its target whenever it is in reach and keeps with the fight, steering for the target only when it lies more than 'beyond' metres further off than the nearest enemy (ruling 226, 4: every ship sent at one point made a knot the enemy fought around).
